mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future earnings, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 1.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of such rate hike events, or the 20-day IC exceeds 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a labor market softening that reduces corporate optimism and pushes S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: IC for the 60-day window remains positive (>0) or SPX 60-day returns are positive in >70% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in the month preceding the decision date, investors anticipate future rate hikes, devaluing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >40% of such events, or IC > 0.02 over the 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over three months indicates weakening supply-side momentum, which raises uncertainty and lowers expected growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >60% of INDPRO contraction periods, or IC < -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive for the first time in three quarters, it signals the end of rate tightening and the onset of rate cutting expectations, which typically precede equity market appreciation over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: 12-month FEDFUNDS change transitions from negative to positive over 3 quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such events, or IC < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and a decline in housing starts (HOUST) suggests labor market softening and reduced construction activity, both of which are associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2% while HOUST decreases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in <30% of such events, or IC > 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: Unexpectedly low retail sales growth (not directly observable in the provided proxies but implied by demand proxies) combined with a sharp drop in consumer confidence indicators (not available) would typically drive negative returns, but here we proxy it with a sharp rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) followed by a decline in manufacturing (GDPC1) indicating demand pullback, resulting in negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% while GDPC1 decreases by >8% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive in >70% of such events, or IC > 0.06.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of monthly new home sales (implied by HOUST) to industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 0.7, it indicates a structural shift toward service-oriented economic activity, which historically precedes S&P 500 positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >80% of such structural shifts, or IC < 0.02 over the 20-day window.
